dek: Set for 25 October 2026 at Dynasty Hotel in Miri, Sarawak, this 22nd-edition charity half marathon is a single-distance 21.1K community run with registration open. Two decades of history in Malaysian Borneo's oil city.
verdict: The 22nd Dynasty Charity Half Marathon is a genuine community institution — twenty-two editions is a remarkable achievement for any race, let alone a single-distance charity half marathon in a secondary Malaysian city. Anchored at Dynasty Hotel Miri, it's a focused, no-frills 21.1K that has outlasted trendier, better-funded events through sheer community loyalty. Miri is Sarawak's northern oil city — the birthplace of Malaysia's petroleum industry — and the gateway to the UNESCO-listed Gunung Mulu National Park and Niah Caves. October in Miri is relatively favourable: the landas (northeast monsoon) typically begins in November, so race conditions are likely to be dry-to-moderate. Registration is open on JomRun. For runners in Sarawak, or those wanting a Borneo charity half marathon with two decades of community roots and real institutional memory, this is a solid, bookable pick. Don't expect slick production — expect a race that has earned its place on the calendar.

sections.heading: 22 Editions: Miri's Charity Institution
paragraphs: Twenty-two editions is an extraordinary run for a community charity race in East Malaysia. [1] Most Malaysian road races last three to five editions before fading; a race that has persisted for over two decades has earned its place through consistency, community trust, and a genuine charitable purpose. The single-distance 21.1K format has remained constant — no dilution into 5K fun runs or corporate relay categories — which speaks to a race that knows what it is and doesn't chase trends.

The charity dimension, while details of the beneficiary aren't always widely publicised, adds a purpose beyond the personal: entry fees and event proceeds support a cause, making every finisher a contributor. [1]

sections.heading: Miri: Borneo's Oil City with World-Heritage Access
paragraphs: Miri is Sarawak's second-largest city, built on the petroleum industry that began with Shell's first well in 1910. [2] It's a practical, working city — not a tourist destination in the Kota Kinabalu mould — but it sits at the doorstep of two UNESCO World Heritage sites: Gunung Mulu National Park (a short flight) and the Niah Caves (about an hour by road). For runners travelling from Peninsular Malaysia or beyond, the race provides a reason to explore Sarawak's northern region — an area off the standard Kuching-KK tourism axis.
Dynasty Hotel Miri provides a practical race hub with parking, accommodation, and facilities built in — the kind of hotel-anchored race that minimises logistical friction. [1]

sections.heading: October Weather: Before the Landas
paragraphs: Sarawak's climate follows a distinct pattern: the landas (northeast monsoon) brings heavy rain from November to March, while the mid-year months are comparatively drier. [3] October sits right at the transition — typically manageable conditions with morning temperatures of 24-26°C and afternoon thunderstorm risk that shouldn't affect a morning race. Humidity is ever-present (80-90% is normal for coastal Borneo), but the pre-landas timing means a reasonable chance of a dry race morning. [2]

sections.heading: What to Expect: Community-Race Realism
paragraphs: Set expectations appropriately. This is a community charity race, not a professionally produced series event. [1] The single-distance format means a focused, committed field — you'll be running alongside locals who have been doing this race for years. Production values will be functional: a timing system, water stations, a finisher medal. Don't expect pace groups, entertainment zones, or expo-scale race-kit collection. What you get instead is authenticity: a race that exists because a community wants it to, not because a commercial sponsor needs brand activation.
